  "anomalies": [
    {
      "category": "wrong_component_type",
      "components": ["R36", "T6", "T2"],
      "pins": ["R36.1", "R36.2", "T6.1", "T2.3"],
      "nets": ["/NET0096", "+3V3"],
      "observed": "R36 is a 10k resistor between the gate node of the main-pump N-MOSFET T6 (IRLR2905, pin G) and +3V3. The same gate node is driven by R28 (100 Ω) from IO10/PUMP_MAIN and by the collector of pre-driver T2 (BT3904). No pull-down to GND exists on this gate. By contrast, the ATO gate (T4) has its gate pulled down to GND by R24 10k.",
      "expected": "The pump N-FET gate should default to OFF (pulled to GND) when the ESP32 pin is high-impedance or during boot. Pulling it up to +3V3 with a 10k resistor lets the main pump switch on whenever IO10 floats and T2 is not pulling the gate low, which is an unsafe default for a pump.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R36\") (pin \"1\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"R36\") (pin \"2\") (pintype \"passive\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"1\") (name \"+3V3\") (class \"Power\")"},
        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R36 /NET0096 +3V3 10k"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "T2 — IRLR2905 (DPAK N-MOSFET) | Main circulation-pump low-side switch | Netlist: drives `PUMP_MAIN` net to the 24 V main pump load; gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) from the ESP32 pin, pre-driven via T1 (BT3904 NPN level shifter)."}
      ],
      "impact": "At power-up or when the firmware leaves IO10 undriven, the gate is held high and the 24 V main circulation pump can run unintentionally. Software-controlled pump gating is also weakened because the gate is biased high, not low.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    }
  ],
  "summary": "Most of the netlist and SPICE connectivity is internally consistent. The one likely deviation is the 10k pull-up R36 on the main-pump MOSFET gate, which is the reverse of the pull-down used on the ATO gate and makes the pump default to ON."
}

anomalies.observed: R36 is a 10k resistor between the gate node of the main-pump N-MOSFET T6 (IRLR2905, pin G) and +3V3. The same gate node is driven by R28 (100 Ω) from IO10/PUMP_MAIN and by the collector of pre-driver T2 (BT3904). No pull-down to GND exists on this gate. By contrast, the ATO gate (T4) has its gate pulled down to GND by R24 10k.
anomalies.expected: The pump N-FET gate should default to OFF (pulled to GND) when the ESP32 pin is high-impedance or during boot. Pulling it up to +3V3 with a 10k resistor lets the main pump switch on whenever IO10 floats and T2 is not pulling the gate low, which is an unsafe default for a pump.

evidence.quote: T2 — IRLR2905 (DPAK N-MOSFET) | Main circulation-pump low-side switch | Netlist: drives `PUMP_MAIN` net to the 24 V main pump load; gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) from the ESP32 pin, pre-driven via T1 (BT3904 NPN level shifter).

anomalies.impact: At power-up or when the firmware leaves IO10 undriven, the gate is held high and the 24 V main circulation pump can run unintentionally. Software-controlled pump gating is also weakened because the gate is biased high, not low.

parsed.summary: Most of the netlist and SPICE connectivity is internally consistent. The one likely deviation is the 10k pull-up R36 on the main-pump MOSFET gate, which is the reverse of the pull-down used on the ATO gate and makes the pump default to ON.
